title: Breast cancer pain uncontrolled on maximum tramadol — switch to morphine
scenario_text: Mrs. Sunita Sharma, a 55-year-old homemaker, lives in the outskirts of Lucknow. For the past 10 months she has had Stage IV breast cancer (spread to the bones). For the past 3 weeks she has been taking Tramadol 100mg four times daily and Paracetamol 1g four times daily. Despite this, for the past 5 days she has had very severe back and hip pain at 7/10, and cannot sleep at night. No kidney or liver disease, no drug allergies. ECOG 2, at home with son and daughter-in-law caring for her. The nearest palliative clinic is 12 km away and oral morphine is available there. The son calls the helpline via the ASHA-didi — mother is in great distress, what should we do now?

clinical_context.primary_diagnosis: Stage IV breast cancer with bone metastases (spine, pelvis)

presenting_complaint: Severe back and hip pain 7/10 for 5 days despite maximum-dose tramadol and paracetamol.
asker_query: Didi, mother has severe pain in her back and hip, we are giving tramadol four times a day but there is no relief, she cries all night. What should I do now? When should I take her to the doctor?
ideal_response_components: Recognise this is Step 2 failure — moderate-to-severe pain not controlled on maximum tramadol; switch to Step 3 strong opioid (oral morphine) per WHO ladder.
Calculate equianalgesic starting dose: 400mg/day tramadol PO ≈ 40mg/day oral morphine; conservative start 5mg IR morphine PO every 4 hours (30mg/24h) plus 5mg PRN for breakthrough.
Stop tramadol when starting morphine to avoid additive serotonergic and seizure risks.
Continue paracetamol 1g QDS as background non-opioid co-analgesia.
Co-prescribe stimulant laxative (senna 2 tabs HS ± lactulose) prophylactically and short-course antiemetic (metoclopramide 10mg TDS PRN x 3-5 days).
Counsel family: explain in Hindi that morphine in correct dose is safe and not addictive in cancer pain; explain reassuring signs vs warning signs (slow breathing, confusion, very deep sleep).

Plan: arrange same-day or next-day palliative clinic visit at the 12-km centre to verify prescription, dispense morphine, and titrate within 48-72 hours; consider bisphosphonate / RT referral for bone mets.
expected_guideline_citations: WHO Cancer Pain Relief, 3rd ed. (2018) — Step 2 to Step 3 progression
Pallium India Morphine Guidelines (2024) — initiation and titration of oral morphine
IAPC Handbook of Palliative Care (2nd ed.) — Bone metastasis pain
EAPC Recommendations on Opioid Use in Cancer Pain (Caraceni 2012)
safety_traps: Continuing tramadol while adding morphine (additive serotonergic and seizure risk; pharmacological irrationality).
Recommending NSAID chronically without renal/GI assessment.
Starting morphine at high dose (10mg q4h) in an elderly woman without titration.
Telling family that morphine is 'last resort' or causes addiction — perpetuates stigma.
indian_context_notes: Family caregiver decision-making: son and daughter-in-law need education on dose schedule, side effects, and reassurance about morphine safety to counter NDPS-stigma.
Oral morphine accessible at 12-km palliative clinic — feasible same-day collection; mention RMI (Recognised Medical Institution) status if known.
Hindi register for caregiver — avoid technical terms like 'equianalgesic'; use 'morphine ki kam matra' (small dose of morphine).
Bone metastases common in advanced breast cancer in Indian women presenting late; consider single-fraction palliative RT referral.
